data.narrative:
Wiliot is a Series C-stage semiconductor company that has raised $364M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Tenstorrent, d-Matrix, Positron AI, DEEPX) valued between $529M and $2.7B, plus 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trading at a median 21.0x price-to-sales.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to derive $619M. Peer-median anchoring across the 4-company private comp set yields $1.5B, reflecting the full observed range of $529M (DEEPX, Series C) to $2.7B (Tenstorrent, Series D). Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be applied without Wiliot's revenue figure, which remains undisclosed. The stage-progression and peer-median methods bracket a triangulated range of $526M (low) to $1.7B (high), with a median of $1.1B across the two applicable approaches.

The analysis supports a valuation in the $1.1B to $1.7B range. Key uncertainties include revenue scale relative to peers, product-market traction, and customer concentration—factors that typically widen dispersion in pre-revenue or early-revenue semiconductor plays. The peer-median estimate ($1.5B) should be weighted as the more robust anchor given direct stage and sector alignment.
